recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-14690 unless the Vocabulary WG separately applies later CodeSystem technical-correction work such as FHIR-54129.
issue_request: FHIR-14690 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for STU3 CodeSystem wording. It asked to improve the introductory bullet so the code system's case-sensitivity property is clearly about the codes it defines, with final resolution text naming version safety, compositional grammar, and whether the defined codes are case sensitive.
initial_application: The issue was pre-applied in SVN revision 13341, imported as git commit 080e47c1a06da8867d5f876ed2bb2d528dc64632. That commit replaced the older bullet, "whether it's case sensitive, version safe, and whether it defines a compositional grammar", with the clarified sentence that says "whether the codes that it defines are case sensitive".
additional_context: The same sentence was intentionally updated three days later by Published/Persuasive with Modification issue FHIR-14243, imported as git commit d8e6a4d5c137f9f46a525457f09d248a8e892a42, replacing the unclear phrase "version safe" with "exhibits concept permanence". CodeSystem is an active resource in source/fhir.ini. Later R6 technical-correction issue FHIR-54129 proposes further edits to this bullet, but it is not Applied/Published and remains outside this default applied/published reconciliation scope.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the authoritative current source keeps the FHIR-14690 case-sensitivity clarification while appropriately reflecting the later FHIR-14243 concept-permanence wording.
